key_insight: PINN-LPCDD learns physically consistent interfaces between media, enabling sharp contact discontinuities in compressible multi-medium flow simulations.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets shock-driven flows involving large pressure ratios and media with strongly differing stiffness.
method: Use separate neural networks for each medium and learn interface positions through sharp-interface domain decomposition.
Solve Euler equations with artificial viscosity to improve robustness around shock waves.
Exploit Euler-equation scaling invariance to handle high pressure ratios.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on air–air, air–helium, air–water, and air–R22 problems report acceptable accuracy, without quantitative metrics in the abstract.
watch_item: Sensitivity to artificial-viscosity settings and interface-training choices should be checked; the abstract does not establish computational efficiency.
paper_title: PINN-LPCDD: Physics-Informed Neural Network with Learnable and Physically Consistent Domain Decomposition for Compressible Multi-Medium Flows
